messages.content:
Return only the shortest standalone answer that preserves every unique fact. No heading, label, preamble, recap or explanation of what the reader should infer. Combine related facts into complete sentences; mention each fact once. Attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Prefer specific verbs and short clauses. Remove redundant implications, repeated subjects and conversational framing. Aim for 35–45 words for verbose material; meaning wins if more are essential.

Preserve every result, condition, exclusion, uncertainty, owner and next action. Preserve exact numbers, units, names, field names, paths, commands, errors, frontmatter and code blocks. Do not claim an instruction happened or an untested result passed. Check all source facts silently before answering.

Already concise: copy EXACTLY. Requested JSON: exact keys/types, no surrounding text. Explicitly requested detail: retain ordered steps, reasons and provenance.

Existing memo edits require requested preview and approved revision-checked memo.write. Stop on conflicts; preserve source evidence. Use one normal drafting call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a standalone handoff memo.

Source:
We have now reached a point where the retry change for the export worker has been implemented, and it is useful to put the present position in writing so that another person can pick up the work. The retry limit was changed from five attempts to three attempts. That is the change that has been made. The relevant unit suite contains 24 tests, and all 24 of those tests passed. There has not yet been a production deployment, so a reader should not interpret the implementation or the passing tests as evidence of deployment. The run that produced the test result is recorded as fixture-run-17. There is still a possibility that the shorter retry budget will make recovery from long network interruptions less likely; that point has not been measured. Mira owns the next step, which is to run the staging interruption test before considering a production deployment. This is the current state of the work rather than a claim that every risk has been removed.

message.content: The export worker retry limit was changed from five attempts to three attempts. The unit suite contains 24 tests, all of which passed (fixture-run-17). There has been no production deployment, so the implementation and passing tests are not evidence of deployment. The shorter retry budget may make recovery from long network interruptions less likely; this has not been measured. Mira owns the next step: run the staging interruption test before considering a production deployment.
